 Dated this the 12th day of November, 2024  ORDER
Petitioner challenges Annexure A5 order.

As per the impugned order, petitioner's application for modification of the bail condition imposed in C.M.P.No.370 of 2024 in C.C.No.798 of 2022 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Kuthuparamba was dismissed.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Kuthuparamba
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Petitioner is an accused alleging commission of offences under Sections 406 and 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 in C.C.No.798 of 2022 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Kuthuparamba.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Kuthuparamba
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The accused is alleged to have collected large amounts of money, promising to secure job visa to the defacto complainant and others at Israel and thereafter failed to provide the employment or return the amount, thus committing the offences alleged.
3. On 23.02.2024, the learned Magistrate enlarged the petitioner on bail on conditions.
One of the conditions stipulated that he shall surrender his passport by 26.02.2024.
However, without surrendering the passport, petitioner sought modification of the said condition in the bail order which was dismissed by order dated 02.04.2024.
Non-bailable warrant has also been issued against the petitioner subsequently.
It is in such circumstances that petitioner has CRL.MC NO. 9456 OF 2024 2024:KER:84053 approached this Court challenging the condition to surrender the passport.

4. I have heard Sri.E.Vijin Karthik, the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as Smt.Sreeja V.,
the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.
The learned Magistrate had imposed a condition directing surrender of his passport on or before 26.02.2024.
Though no orders had been produced to indicate that any extension of time was granted, petitioner contend that time was extended by one month.

Despite the above extension,
petitioner failed to surrender the passport and instead sought modification of the bail condition which was dismissed.
In the above circumstances, I am of the view that the challenge against Annexure A5 does not hold good since the petitioner had willingly accepted the conditions imposed by the learned Magistrate.
Moreover, the condition to surrender the passport cannot be said to be onerous in the circumstances as the petitioner is alleged to have committed a visa fraud.
Under no circumstances, can the petitioner be permitted to violate the conditions imposed by the court as his liberty was made dependent upon the said condition.

Therefore, the learned Magistrate was totally Anil Jose vs State Of Kerala on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44835307/
2 justified in dismissing the application for modification of the bail condition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. However, the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that now the petitioner is wiling to surrender the passport to the court on or before 14.11.2024.
He also submits that he is unable to approach the court to surrender the passport as he apprehends that he would be remanded to custody due to the warrant issued against him.

Taking note of the above submission, I am of the view that if the petitioner surrenders his passport, the learned Magistrate ought to consider the application for recall of warrant and for grant of bail preferably on the same day itself.

Accordingly, while declining to interfere with the condition of bail imposed in Annexure A4 order,
there will be a direction to the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Kuthuparamba to consider the application for recall of warrant and for grant of bail, if any filed by the petitioner in C.C.No.798 of 2022, preferably on the same day itself, provided the petitioner surrenders the passport and appears before the court on or before 14.11.2024.
